stories.headline: Alibaba Releases Qwen3.5-Omni, Claims 215 SOTA Wins Over Gemini 3.1 Pro

key_facts.fact: Alibaba released Qwen3.5-Omni, a fully omnimodal LLM supporting text, image, audio, and video understanding plus text and speech generation.
key_facts.excerpt: Qwen3.5-Omni is Qwen's latest generation of fully omnimodal LLM, supporting the understanding of text, images, audio, and audio-visual content.

key_facts.fact: The Plus variant claims to surpass Gemini 3.1 Pro on audio benchmarks and achieves 215 state-of-the-art results across benchmarks.
key_facts.excerpt: Alibaba Qwen 3.5-Omni Outperforms Gemini 3.1 Pro Across 215 Benchmarks

key_facts.fact: The model supports over 10 hours of audio input and features audio-visual vibe coding, where users can point a camera at something and describe what they want built.
key_facts.excerpt: Qwen3.5-Omni might be the strongest multimodal frontier model right now. What impressed me most: audio-visual vibe coding. Point your camera at something, describe what you want, and it turns that into code.

key_facts.fact: The model includes real-time web search capabilities built in.
key_facts.excerpt: 'Qwen3.5-Omni' has been released, enabling text generation, code generation, image recognition, speech synthesis, and web search.

stories.headline: California Gov. Newsom Signs First-of-Its-Kind AI Safety and Privacy Executive Order

key_facts.fact: Governor Newsom signed an executive order requiring AI companies contracting with California to demonstrate responsible policies and meet rigorous privacy and security standards.
key_facts.excerpt: Governor Gavin Newsom issued an executive order today to strengthen California's procurement processes and raise the bar for artificial intelligence companies seeking to do business with the state.

key_facts.fact: The order is framed as a contrast to the Trump administration, which has been rolling back federal AI protections and contracting standards.
key_facts.excerpt: While the federal government dismantles contracting standards and removes basic protections for Americans, Governor Gavin Newsom today issued an executive order to explore stronger AI standards for state procurement.

key_facts.fact: The order also commits to expanding California's use of GenAI to deliver improved state services, including a new AI-directed tool to help Californians navigate government.
key_facts.excerpt: The order also commits to expanding California's use of GenAI to help deliver improved state services, including a new AI-directed tool to help Californians navigate government.

key_facts.fact: California is described as the 4th largest economy in the world, making its procurement standards significant for the AI industry.
key_facts.excerpt: California remains committed to ensuring that AI solutions adopted and deployed by the largest state in the nation and 4th largest economy in the world cannot be misused by bad actors.

stories.headline: Microsoft Launches Copilot Cowork and Multi-Model Critique System Using Claude and GPT

key_facts.fact: Microsoft rolled out Copilot Cowork to its Frontier early access program, enabling long-running, multi-step tasks with tool use, file access, calendar planning, and daily briefings.
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft is making 'Copilot Cowork' more widely available and launching a new AI research agent. The previously announced feature lets the system handle multi-step tasks using tools, accessing and outputting files.

key_facts.fact: The new Critique feature has one AI model (Claude) draft research while a second model (GPT) reviews it, pulling from both Anthropic and OpenAI models.
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft's 'Researcher' tool now has a 'Critique' function where one AI model writes a draft and a second one reviews it. It pulls from both Anthropic and OpenAI models.

key_facts.fact: Microsoft claims the Critique agent outperforms Perplexity with Claude Opus 4.6 by 7 points on deep research benchmarks, though it doesn't compare against OpenAI's GPT-5-based Deep Research.
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft says the new agent hits best-in-class deep research performance and outperforms Perplexity with Claude Opus 4.6 by 7 points. Microsoft's benchmark doesn't include a comparison with OpenAI's new GPT-5-based Deep Research, though.

key_facts.fact: A new Model Council feature lets users compare answers from different AI models side by side to see where they agree or differ.
key_facts.excerpt: There's also a new 'Model Council' feature where users can compare answers from different AI models side by side to see where they agree or differ.

stories.headline: GitHub Copilot Injected Ads Into 11,000+ Pull Requests, Disabled After Backlash

key_facts.fact: GitHub Copilot was found injecting promotional 'product tips' referencing Raycast into pull request descriptions, with the same text found in over 11,000 pull requests.
key_facts.excerpt: A developer asked GitHub Copilot to fix a typo in a pull request. Copilot fixed the typo, then edited the PR description to include an advertisement for itself and Raycast. The same promotional text has been found in over 11,000 pull requests.

key_facts.fact: After widespread developer backlash, GitHub disabled product tips entirely, with product manager Martin Woodward calling it a mistake rather than paid advertising.
key_facts.excerpt: Following backlash from developers, GitHub has removed Copilot's ability to stick ads - what it calls 'tips' - into pull requests.

key_facts.fact: GitHub explained the tips were originally included in Copilot-originated PRs but expanded problematically when Copilot gained the ability to work on any PR.
key_facts.excerpt: Basically it was giving product tips which was kinda ok on Copilot originated PR's but then when we added the ability to have Copilot work on any PR by mentioning it, it started appearing on non-Copilot PRs.

sources.title: Microsoft's AI slop is infecting GitHub: Copilot is now injecting ads into pull requests
GitHub backs down, kills Copilot pull-request ads after backlash

key_facts.fact: 55% of Americans say AI will do more harm than good in their day-to-day lives, and 80% are 'very concerned' or 'somewhat concerned' about AI.
key_facts.excerpt: As artificial intelligence continues to evolve, 55% say AI will do more harm than good in their day-to-day lives.

key_facts.fact: 65% oppose building data centers in their community, with 72% of opponents citing electricity costs as a key concern.
key_facts.excerpt: 65% oppose building data centers in their community. 72% of those opposing data centers pointed to electricity costs.

key_facts.fact: Nearly 70% think AI will cut jobs, with Gen Z the most pessimistic generation about AI's impact on employment.
key_facts.excerpt: Nearly 70% think AI will cut jobs with Gen Z most pessimistic.

key_facts.fact: AI job loss concerns are shared roughly equally between blue collar (73%) and white collar (71%) workers.
key_facts.excerpt: AI job loss concerns are shared roughly equally for blue collar and white collar workers (73% vs 71%).

stories.headline: OpenAI Launches AI Safety Bug Bounty With Up to $7,500 Payouts

key_facts.fact: OpenAI introduced a new Safety Bug Bounty program paying up to $7,500 for AI-specific safety vulnerabilities, including harmful model behavior at scale and proprietary information leaks.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI have introduced a new bug bounty programme focused on AI-specific safety scenarios, with researchers potentially seeing payouts of up to $7,500 for vulnerabilities found in the AI firm's agentic products.

key_facts.fact: The program targets agentic products including the Atlas Browser and Codex vibe-coding agent, as well as MCP (Model Context Protocol) integrations.
key_facts.excerpt: The new programme encourages researchers to hunt for safety flaws in the company's flagship agentic products, such as the Atlas Browser or the Codex vibe-coding agent. Bounties can also be won by finding vulnerabilities in Connectors and MCP integrations.

key_facts.fact: The Safety Bug Bounty complements OpenAI's existing Security Bug Bounty which has maximum rewards of $100,000 and has paid out on 417 bugs.
key_facts.excerpt: Designed to complement OpenAI's Security Bug Bounty, which has maximum rewards of $100,000. As for the Security Bug Bounty, that is currently sitting at 417 reward-earning bugs found.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI is specifically looking for MCP vulnerabilities where systems can be tricked, misconfigured, or bypassed to cause unauthorized data access or impersonated actions.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI is looking for MCP vulnerabilities that let these systems be tricked, misconfigured, or bypassed in ways that cause real-world harm, such as unauthorised data access or actions being carried out under someone else's account.

stories.headline: Meta Releases Hyperagents, an AI Framework That Can Rewrite Its Own Code

key_facts.fact: Meta released Hyperagents, a framework that unifies task-solving and meta-improvement into a single editable Python program, enabling AI agents to autonomously modify their own source code.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta has just released Hyperagents, an innovative AI framework that enables autonomous self-modification. By uniting task-solving and meta-improvement into a single, editable Python program, Hyperagents can enhance both their task performance and self-improvement strategies.

key_facts.fact: Hyperagents extend the Darwin Godel Machine (DGM) by making all meta-procedures editable, allowing the meta agent to rewrite its own modification code, solving infinite meta-level regress.
key_facts.excerpt: The concept is simple to state and profound in implication: AI agents that can modify their own source code. This creates a self-referential loop.

key_facts.fact: The system is domain-agnostic, demonstrating improved performance across robotics, math grading, and academic paper review without task-specific alignment.
key_facts.excerpt: This breakthrough promises domain-agnostic scalability, transforming fields from robotics to paper review without predefined limits.

key_facts.fact: The system runs over 100 experiments per iteration using LLM-driven latent-space search to iteratively optimize its code.
key_facts.excerpt: The system undergoes extensive experimental runs — over a hundred per iteration — aimed at refining its capabilities.

sources.title: Meta Unveils Hyperagents: The AI Framework That Rewrites Its Own Rules
HyperAgents Explained: Self-Improving AI Systems from Meta Research

stories.headline: Google Releases Agent Development Kit for Java 1.0 With A2A Protocol Support

key_facts.fact: Google released version 1.0.0 of the Agent Development Kit (ADK) for Java, expanding the multi-language ADK ecosystem (Python, Java, Go, TypeScript).
key_facts.excerpt: What started with Python has now grown into a multi-language ecosystem: Python, Java, Go and Typescript. Today, we're happy to announce the release of version 1.0.0 of ADK for Java.

key_facts.fact: Key features include Google Maps and URL context grounding tools, a centralized plugin architecture, event compaction for context window management, and Human-in-the-Loop workflows.
key_facts.excerpt: New powerful tools includes new grounding capabilities like the GoogleMapsTool and the UrlContextTool. A new App container manages Plugins for global execution control. Introduces event compaction to manage context window sizes. Supports ToolConfirmation workflows.

key_facts.fact: The release includes native support for the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol, enabling agents built in different languages and frameworks to communicate seamlessly.
key_facts.excerpt: ADK for Java now natively supports the official Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol, allowing your ADK agents to seamlessly communicate with remote agents built in any language or framework.

sources.title: Announcing ADK for Java 1.0.0: Building the Future of AI Agents in Java
